summary.text: Max Burchett is the Democratic candidate for Oklahoma House of Representatives District 33 in the November 3, 2026 general election, where he faces Republican incumbent Molly Jenkins.
A pharmacist and technology executive, he is chief information officer of the Oklahoma City Indian Clinic and says he is running on health care access, education and technology policy.

paragraphs.text: Burchett graduated from Bartlesville High School, and Ballotpedia lists degrees from Southwestern Oklahoma State University in 2013 and Oklahoma State University in 2016.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he described himself as a healthcare executive, pharmacist, technology leader, husband and father with a background in healthcare administration, clinical pharmacy and information technology.
He said that as chief information officer of the Oklahoma City Indian Clinic he has led modernization, cybersecurity and operational improvement initiatives.
Burchett's Democratic primary was canceled, and he advanced to the general election without appearing on the primary ballot.

He said his campaign messages include practical problem-solving over partisanship, reducing administrative barriers and strengthening rural and underserved health care, and supporting schools, infrastructure investment and workforce development.
